watch_items.item: Workplace Relations Legislation Amendment (Building Cooperative Workplaces No. 1) Act 2026 (No. 62)
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Assent 6 Jul 2026, effect 7 Jul 2026: FWC process reforms (general protections and unlawful termination disputes without a threshold dismissal finding, on-the-papers determinations by consent, dismissal of vexatious applications and repeat-applicant bars, delegated certificates), road transport contractor rights, Commonwealth procurement preferencing, supported and intractable bargaining changes. The 'No. 1' title implies a further tranche
watch_items.expected_trigger: A 'No. 2' Bill; further Fair Work Commission Rules amendments (Fair Work Commission Amendment (2026 Measures No. 1) Rules 2026, F2026L00987, already made)

watch_items.item: Proposed Commonwealth restrictions on non-compete and other worker restraints
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Position at 26 August 2026: Treasury states the reforms should take effect from 2027 following consultation and passage; consultation closed 5 Sep 2025; no exposure draft or Bill located at that snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Bill introduction/passage; enacted commencement and provision-specific application rules; no fixed 2027 start assumed
watch_items.status_at_review: Announced/proposed only. The Treasury exposure draft consultation closed 2 Oct 2026 (reported). No Bill introduced into Parliament was located at the 28 Oct 2026 review. The 13 Oct 2026 reading of the exposure draft still governs: draft cl 2 proposes commencement on the first 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October after Royal Assent, not a fixed 2027 start; proposed ss 333Z and 333ZA tie the ban to annualised full-time equivalent earnings at or below the high income threshold and cover casuals and pieceworkers irrespective of it; proposed ss 333ZF-333ZH prohibit co-worker non-solicitation terms; proposed s 333ZJ(5) restricts cascading restraints; Schedule 1 extends cartel provisions to no-poach and wage-fixing arrangements; application cl 143 must be read provision by provision. No enacted Act or legal start date confirmed.
watch_items.review_basis: Official Treasury-hosted exposure draft PDF inspected on 2026-10-13 (draft content only); Bill-introduction status from web search on 2026-10-28, not from aph.gov.au. Recheck Parliament and legislation.gov.au at use.

watch_items.item: Working from home term in the Clerks - Private Sector Award 2020 (AM2024/34)
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Not on the register at the 26 August 2026 snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Operation of clause 5A from 26 Oct 2026 (reported); any FWC dispute decisions under the award dispute clause; any extension of the term to other awards
watch_items.status_at_review: Reported (secondary sources, 28 Oct 2026 review): a Full Bench (AM2024/34; reported citation [2026] FWCFB 281, 19 Oct 2026) made the final determination inserting clause 5A 'Requests for working from home arrangements' into the Clerks - Private Sector Award 2020, operative 26 Oct 2026. As reported, a request must be in writing and specify the days or pattern of days; the employer and employee may agree to modify specified award terms; agreement must be free of coercion or duress; disputes may go to the award dispute clause; and the clause sets no response time, reasons requirement or refusal grounds (the Full Bench did not adopt a union right-to-request model). Section 65 flexible working requests remain available to eligible employees. The fwc.gov.au news page still shows only the 27 Aug 2026 draft-determination stage, and the Fair Work Ombudsman page on the new rules was seen only as a search title
watch_items.review_basis: Secondary sources only; the final determination, its citation and operative date were not read on fwc.gov.au. Confirm against the determination and the current award text before relying on it
